summary: SM UB-18 was a German Type UB II submarine (U-boat) in the German Imperial Navy during World War I. It was ordered on 30 April 1915, launched on 21 August 1915, and commissioned on 11 December 1915. The note says it sank 126 ships in 31 patrols, making it the 13th most successful U-boat in both world wars, before being rammed and sunk by the trawler Ben Lawer in the English Channel on 9 December 1917.
one_line: SM UB-18 was a German WWI Type UB II U-boat that sank 126 ships before being sunk by the trawler Ben Lawer in 1917.
key_facts: SM UB-18 was a German Type UB II submarine, also called a U-boat, in the German Imperial Navy during World War I.
SM UB-18 was ordered on 30 April 1915.
SM UB-18 was launched on 21 August 1915.
SM UB-18 was commissioned into the German Imperial Navy on 11 December 1915.
The submarine SM UB-18 sank 126 ships in 31 patrols.
SM UB-18 is listed as the 13th most successful U-boat in both world wars.
SM UB-18 was rammed by the trawler Ben Lawer.
SM UB-18 was sunk in the English Channel on 9 December 1917 after being rammed by the trawler Ben Lawer.
